extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: LongBench is a bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding in large language models (LLMs). It comprises 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese, with an average length of 6,711 words (English) and 13,386 characters (Chinese). The tasks cover key long-text application areas including single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion. All datasets are standardized into a unified format for effortless automatic evaluation of LLMs.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li
extraction.publisher: Tsinghua University, Zhipu.AI, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
extraction.citeAs: LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongBench datasets were collected from a variety of sources, including public datasets (e.g., NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, GovReport, QMSum, MultiNews, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, LSHT, LCC, RepoBench-P), manually curated datasets (e.g., MultiFieldQA-en, MultiFieldQA-zh, VCSUM), and synthetic datasets (e.g., PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en, PassageRetrieval-zh). The data collection process involved extracting test instances from public datasets, manually curating new datasets, and designing synthetic tasks to test specific long-context scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Experiments, Synthetic Data Generation
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public datasets (e.g., NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, GovReport, QMSum, MultiNews, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, LSHT, LCC, RepoBench-P), Wikipedia, C4 Dataset, Arxiv, Chinese Judgements Online, Chinese Government Website, GitHub repositories
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Datasets were standardized into a unified format. For public datasets, test instances were extracted to avoid test leakage. For MultiFieldQA datasets, documents were collected from multiple sources (e.g., legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, academic papers) and annotated by Ph.D. students. Synthetic tasks were designed to test specific long-context scenarios (e.g., PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en, PassageRetrieval-zh). Code completion datasets were adapted to include repository-level context.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created by Ph.D. students for MultiFieldQA datasets, ensuring definitive answers for automated evaluation. For synthetic tasks, annotations were generated using GPT-3.5-Turbo. For code completion tasks, annotations were derived from GitHub repositories.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Manual annotation by Ph.D. students for MultiFieldQA datasets; GPT-3.5-Turbo for synthetic tasks; GitHub repositories for code completion tasks
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-validation among annotators for MultiFieldQA datasets showed a 100% accuracy rate of the annotated answers. For synthetic tasks, the performance was evaluated using exact match accuracy.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 (for most datasets); 3 (for MultiFieldQA datasets, as annotated by three Ph.D. students)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Ph.D. students with extensive research experience in NLP; specific demographics not provided
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available on GitHub (https://github.com/THUDM/LongBench) and is maintained by Tsinghua University, Zhipu.AI, and the Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Versioning information and deprecation policies are not explicitly stated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: LongBench aims to facilitate research in long context understanding for large language models, which could have broad applications in fields such as document analysis, code completion, and question answering. The benchmark is designed to evaluate models' ability to handle long sequences, which is crucial for real-world applications involving books, reports, and codebases.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential biases may exist in the datasets derived from public sources (e.g., Wikipedia, Arxiv, GitHub), as these sources may reflect inherent biases in the data they contain. For example, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, and MuSiQue are derived from Wikipedia, which may introduce biases related to the content and structure of Wikipedia articles.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: 1) Potentially unreliable automatic metrics (e.g., ROUGE-L, F1) may not accurately reflect the quality of responses, especially for models generating longer responses. 2) Coupling with instruction-following capabilities: Performance on LongBench is influenced by models' instruction-following abilities. 3) Memorization vs. context understanding: Some tasks may rely on memorization rather than long context understanding, as evidenced by the performance of models when context is withheld. 4) Limited generalization: The benchmark may not fully capture the diversity of real-world long-context scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine-tuning for large language models (LLMs) to evaluate their long context understanding capabilities. The benchmark is designed to assess models' ability to handle long sequences in tasks such as single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion.
